Today we are learning the area of a rectangle. Area measures the surface enclosed by a shape.
Suppose a rectangle has length l and width w. We divide it into unit squares to derive the general rule.
Each row contains l squares and there are w rows, therefore area equals l times w. This is a formula for every rectangle.
A student asks why area is measured in square units. Because we count two-dimensional unit squares, not lengths.
Exercise one: a garden is 7 metres long and 3 metres wide. Find its area and then its perimeter.
For this garden the given length is 7 and width is 3. First write A equals l times w.
Why multiply here? The garden has three rows of seven unit squares. This explains the calculation for our garden.
Seven times three is 21, so the answer to the first part is 21 square metres.
Isi question ka second part perimeter hai. Add all four sides: 7 plus 3 plus 7 plus 3.
The garden's perimeter is 20 metres. Both parts of exercise one are now solved.

Back to the general concept: perimeter measures a boundary, while area measures the enclosed surface.
A conceptual doubt: can area be negative? A physical area is nonnegative because it measures surface size.
